summary: Windows x64 build of the same app (Tauri 2 shell + PyInstaller one-dir backend) produced by GitHub Actions, plus a release workflow; macOS arm64 build unchanged. Cross-platform lock/data-dir helper, Rust cfg(windows) paths, NSIS config, release docs and ADR 0040.
scope_note: Worktree windows-release from main ffe4836. Release/build path, IPC-adjacent Rust shell and lock code, hence critical. The Windows code could not be compiled or run here (no Windows host, no network); CI is the first verification.

budget_impact.rationale: Packaging, file locking and paths only; no model call, prompt, retry, network call or data leaving the machine. CI builds use no secrets.
budget_impact.after: macOS and Windows x64 builds; same zero-token core

additional_checks.scope: macOS Rust path only; Windows cfg blocks not compiled

open_risks: Independent review not done; critical path (release/build, shell, locks).

cfg(windows) Rust, rfd 0.15 (new crate, default-features off), Cargo.lock not updated offline, NSIS/WebView2 embedBootstrapper, PyInstaller --add-data os.pathsep and the msvcrt lock are uncompiled/unrun on Windows.
Unsigned installers: SmartScreen and antivirus may block; WebView2 runtime download needs network when the system lacks it.
Windows key files have no 0600; protection is the per-user profile ACL.
Windows unit-test run is untested; POSIX-only tests are skipped explicitly, others may still fail.
Third-party actions use major-version tags, not commit SHAs (follow-up).
Backend stderr is NUL on Windows (no log file); the organization worker subprocess has no CREATE_NO_WINDOW flag of its own (inherits the hidden console).
